title: Bilge Activity After Rainy Nights
dataSources: NMEA/SignalK data (`nmea:reading`), bilge pump (`bilge:event`), mooring/anchor watch (`mooring:status`), marine weather (`marineweather:forecast`).
app: Marine electronics — NMEA 2000 / SignalK boat networks, bilge, battery and shore-power sensors, anchor-watch GPS, and marine weather feeds — streamed to Splunk HEC via SignalK and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=bilge:event rain_window=true
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as pump_cycles by _time
| sort - _time
description: Shows whether rainy nights correlate with more bilge-pump activity the next day.
value: This is a simple way to spot weather-linked leaks before they become a much more expensive surprise.
implementation: Tag bilge events that follow rainy windows; track daily pump-cycle counts in `index=personal`.
visualization: Daily chart of bilge-pump cycles after rainy nights.
grandmaExplanation: It spots whether rainy nights seem to lead to more bilge pumping, which can hint at leaks or water getting in where it should not.
